paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where “Base” denotes LLM without editing.
model_annotation: This plot illustrates the performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, comparing the accuracy of various models across a range of co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis represents the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, ranging from approximately 3 to 3,000, with tick labels at 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis represents the accuracy (ACC) as a percentage on a linear scale, ranging from 40% to 65%, with tick labels at 5% intervals. The plot displays six lines, each representing a different editing method: Base (black, circle marker, solid line), FT (blue, triangle marker, solid line), IKE (red, triangle marker, solid line), MEND (brown, diamond marker, solid line), MEMIT (purple, triangle marker, solid line), and ROME (green, square marker, solid line). The Base model starts at around 39% accuracy and increases to approximately 45% as the co-occurrence number rises from 3 to 3,000. The FT model begins at around 40% and reaches about 49% over the same range. The IKE model starts at roughly 43% and ends at approximately 50%. The MEND model begins at around 45% and increases to about 57%. The MEMIT model starts at approximately 41% and rises to around 55%. The ROME model begins at roughly 51% and reaches about 66%. All models exhibit an overall increasing trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases.
